P001.text: Treat the conflicting evidence at the two branches as a mixture of potentially distinguishable demand components: for example, needs that weekday access serves, needs that weekend access could serve, and needs constrained by transport, school calendars or other barriers.

P002.text: These are hypotheses, not established groups.

P003.text: The moving-phase counterpart is the recurring sequence of opening opportunities through which potential visits can proceed; the stationary-phase counterpart is the relatively persistent set of access constraints that can delay or prevent participation.

P004.text: Assume repeated exposure to these opportunities may produce different uptake patterns; attendance and stated unmet need need not move together.

P005.text: Propose a reversible three-month trial at both branches, transferring specified weekday blocks to specified weekend blocks.

P006.text: Before launch, verify that coverage, pay premiums, preparation and recovery time fit the existing staffing budget; do not launch an infeasible schedule.

P007.text: Document the original schedule and restoration procedure.

P008.text: Establish comparable pre-trial measurements and, where available, unchanged opening windows as contextual comparisons.

P009.text: Repeatedly expose demand to the trial schedule over weekly cycles: potential visits may proceed into attendance or remain deferred or unserved, the counterpart of repeated partitioning.

P010.text: Keep the schedule stable within each assessment period, and log transport service, school term, programming and any schedule changes.

P011.text: Collect hourly door counts, program attendance, brief voluntary questions about alternative visit times and unmet needs, and staff workload reports.

P012.text: Measure removed weekday blocks through their baseline use and subsequent reports of lost access.

P013.text: Before launch, set explicit numerical criteria for meaningful access gains, tolerable weekday access loss and staff workload, plus review dates and immediate safety or coverage stopping rules; the packet supplies no values.

P014.text: Review weekly for operating breaches, at a preannounced midpoint for adjustments, and at three months for the final decision.

P015.text: Treat any adjustment as a new operating condition.

P016.text: Look for recurring differences in when and under which conditions demand becomes observable: weekend uptake, concentration around transport arrivals or programs, delayed uptake across weeks, continued weekday use, and persistent reports of inability to attend.

P017.text: These time-and-condition profiles are the counterparts of separated bands or peaks; relative delay before uptake is the retention counterpart.

P018.text: Report branches, program and ordinary visits, and term and transport conditions separately where sample sizes permit.

P019.text: Show counts and rates per open hour alongside uncertainty and workload.

P020.text: Do not add program attendance to door counts when the same visits may be counted twice, or interpret an unobserved visit as directly measured unmet demand.

P021.text: Repeatable differences in uptake or continued deferral would support distinguishable access-response components and characterize their relative responsiveness or delay under this schedule.

P022.text: Convergent voluntary reports can help distinguish newly enabled access from visits merely shifted from weekdays.

P023.text: Keep the trial schedule only if the precommitted access-gain criterion is met, weekday losses and workload remain within limits, and the budget remains feasible.

P024.text: Change particular blocks if a reproducible profile suggests a better allocation; state the hypothesis and measure again under the revised conditions.

P025.text: Stop or restore the original schedule on an immediate stopping-rule breach, or at the final review if gains fail the agreed criterion or harms exceed limits.

P026.text: If evidence remains inconclusive, report that uncertainty and restore the original schedule unless a further bounded trial is explicitly authorized.

P027.text: Different needs can produce the same attendance profile, analogous to co-elution; one person can also contribute to several profiles.

P028.text: Transport changes, school terms, programming, weather and adjustment time can shift apparent retention.

P029.text: Door counts, program attendance, survey responses and workload reports are nonspecific and differently selected signals.

P030.text: Attendance timing alone cannot identify a demand group's needs, prove previously unmet demand or establish that the schedule caused a change.

P031.text: Seek corroboration through direct accounts of access barriers, transport information and comparable observation periods; unchanged windows offer context but may themselves receive displaced visits.

P032.text: Sparse or contradictory evidence warrants unresolved components, not invented separation.

P033.text: A three-month result supports decisions only for the conditions observed; retaining the schedule should include a review when materially different seasonal conditions arrive.
